another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'd like to claim for my son Alex. He's 13 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex!

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I have a few more questions:

Are you responsible for Alex? This could mean he lives with you, or you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards his upkeep (such as paying for food, clothes, or pocket money).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me - I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

Next, could you tell me about your residency status? Are you currently living in the UK (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not living in the UK at the moment - I live abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

Since you're living abroad, I need to ask a few more questions to understand your situation better.

Are you currently working for the UK government or serving in the UK armed forces while living abroad?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not working for the UK government or serving in the armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

One more question about your circumstances: Are you a national of an EEA country (European Economic Area) or Switzerland, and are you or a family member working in the UK while you live abroad?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not an EEA or Swiss national, and nobody in my family is working in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all of this information.

Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not currently eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's a summary of the assessment:

**For Alex:**
- ✅ Alex is under 16, so he meets the age requirement
- ✅ You are responsible for Alex as he lives with you
- ❌ **Residency requirement not met** – You are living abroad and don't qualify for any of the exceptions

**Why the residency matters:**
To claim Child Benefit, you generally need to be living in the UK. There are some exceptions for people living abroad, such as:
- UK government employees working overseas
- Members of the UK armed forces
- EEA/Swiss nationals with certain work connections to the UK

Unfortunately, none of these exceptions apply to your situation.

**What you could do:**
If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if you return to live in the UK), you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit at that time.

I hope this information is helpful. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
